headline: Central bank to provide cash injection for Islami Bank to resolve liquidity crisis
summary: Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman assures depositors that they will be able to withdraw their funds freely in the next few days.
details: Bangladesh Bank has confirmed it will provide a cash injection to Islami Bank Bangladesh to resolve a liquidity crisis that has seen over Tk 30 billion in deposits withdrawn.
Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman stated at a post-budget press conference in Dhaka that the existing cash crisis will be resolved in a few days, ensuring depositors can withdraw their funds freely.
The trouble began after the central bank appointed Khurshid Alam as chairman of the bank's board of directors on May 24, leading to street protests and parliamentary debates.
Islami Bank had requested Tk 100 billion in liquidity support from the central bank on June 9, citing increasing pressure on cash withdrawals.
Governor Rahman also denied rumors of illegal government interference in the bank's internal affairs, stating that the central bank has not dictated loans, promotions, or transfers.
caption:
Over Tk 30 billion has been withdrawn from Islami Bank. Now, the central bank steps in with a cash injection to save the lender.

Bangladesh Bank has confirmed it will provide a cash injection to Islami Bank Bangladesh to resolve a liquidity crisis that has seen over Tk 30 billion in deposits withdrawn.

Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman stated at a post-budget press conference in Dhaka that the existing cash crisis will be resolved in a few days, ensuring depositors can withdraw their funds freely.

The trouble began after the central bank appointed Khurshid Alam as chairman of the bank's board of directors on May 24, leading to street protests and parliamentary debates.

Islami Bank had requested Tk 100 billion in liquidity support from the central bank on June 9, citing increasing pressure on cash withdrawals.

Governor Rahman also denied rumors of illegal government interference in the bank's internal affairs, stating that the central bank has not dictated loans, promotions, or transfers.

headline_marked: 4 [[four people killed by trains]] in Dhaka in 3 days
headline: 4 four people killed by trains in Dhaka in 3 days
summary: Three of the victims were women; police are working to identify the remaining three unidentified bodies.
details: Four people, including three women, were killed in separate train accidents in Dhaka over the last three days from Wednesday to Friday morning.
On Wednesday night, the body of a 25-year-old man named Aslamul from Pirojpur Sadar upazila was recovered from the area between Kaola rail crossing and the Airport outpost.
On the same night, the body of an unidentified woman, estimated to be over 30 years old, was recovered from a nearby area.
On Thursday morning, another unidentified woman, estimated to be over 50 years old, was killed by a train on the same rail line.
On Friday morning, the body of an elderly woman, estimated to be over 70 years old, was recovered from beside the railway tracks in the Uttara Kotbari area.
According to Sub-Inspector Mohammad Abdur Razzaq of the Railway Police Airport outpost, all four victims died on the spot.
The police have identified Aslamul through fingerprint matching, while the identification of the other three women remains pending.
All four bodies have undergone autopsy at the Dhaka Medical College morgue on Friday.
